rules.quote: It sends and receives bytes on a serial line in 8N1 format. 8N1 framing: one start bit (0), eight data bits with the least significant bit first, no parity, one stop bit (1).
rules.statement: Serial frames use 8N1: one start bit (0), eight data bits LSB first, no parity, one stop bit (1).

review.reason: Quote states 8N1 framing explicitly; checkable.

rules.quote: The bit period is a fixed number of i_clk cycles, set by a parameter. Bit period of PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT clock cycles.
rules.statement: Each bit period lasts PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT i_clk cycles.

review.reason: Quote states bit period equals PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT clocks.

rules.quote: The line is high when idle.
rules.condition: When the serial line is idle
rules.statement: The serial line is held high when idle.

review.reason: Idle line high is stated and checkable.

rules.quote: The parameter is fixed at elaboration and its legal range is 4 to 65535.
rules.statement: PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT is fixed at elaboration and must be within the legal range 4 to 65535.

review.reason: Parameter legal range is a constraint on configuration, not a runtime-checkable behaviour; strength fine but actor is the integrator/configuration. Not checkable by assertion or scenario.

rules.quote: Bytes sent back to back have no idle bit between the stop bit and the next start bit.
rules.condition: When bytes are sent back to back
rules.statement: No idle bit is inserted between the stop bit and the next start bit.

review.reason: Back-to-back transmission without idle bit is stated and checkable.

rules.quote: A one-byte holding register keeps each received byte until it is taken.
rules.statement: A one-byte holding register keeps each received byte until it is taken.

review.reason: Holding register retaining byte until taken is observable behaviour at o_rx_data/o_rx_valid.

rules.quote: Start-bit detection on a falling edge, a second start-bit check in the middle of the bit (glitch rejection), and sampling of every data bit and the stop bit in the middle of the bit.
rules.statement: The receiver detects a start bit on a falling edge and rechecks the start bit in the middle of the bit, rejecting glitches.

review.reason: Start detection on falling edge and mid-bit recheck with glitch rejection is stated; scenario with glitches.

rules.quote: Start-bit detection on a falling edge, a second start-bit check in the middle of the bit (glitch rejection), and sampling of every data bit and the stop bit in the middle of the bit.
rules.statement: The receiver samples each data bit and the stop bit in the middle of the bit.

review.reason: Mid-bit sampling is stated, but it is the same sentence as UL-1.2-07; kept as separate behaviour but check should be both is not needed; scenario is fine. Strength/actor OK.

rules.quote: A frame error flag (stop bit sampled as 0), delivered together with the byte.
rules.condition: When the stop bit is sampled as 0
rules.statement: o_rx_frame_err is set and delivered together with the received byte.

review.reason: Frame error flag when stop sampled 0, delivered with the byte; stated.

rules.quote: An overrun pulse (o_rx_overrun) when a received byte is dropped because the previous byte has not been taken.
rules.condition: When a received byte is dropped because the previous byte has not been taken
rules.statement: o_rx_overrun pulses.

review.reason: Overrun pulse when a byte is dropped is stated.

rules.quote: Full duplex: the transmitter and the receiver work at the same time and do not depend on each other.
rules.statement: The transmitter and receiver operate simultaneously and independently of each other (full duplex).

review.reason: Full duplex independence stated; scenario test.

rules.quote: Parameter: PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT; Default: 16; Legal values: 4 to 65535; Description: Bit period in i_clk cycles (N), used by the transmitter and the receiver
rules.statement: PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT defines the bit period N in i_clk cycles for both transmitter and receiver, default 16, legal range 4 to 65535.

review.reason: Quote states parameter meaning, default and legal range; legal range/usage is exercisable via scenarios.

rules.quote: Parameter: LPARA_UART_HALF_BIT; Default: Derived; Legal values: -; Description: PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT / 2 with integer division (floor); the middle-of-bit sampling offset H [REQ-PAR-002] LPARA_UART_HALF_BIT shall equal floor(PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT / 2).
rules.statement: LPARA_UART_HALF_BIT shall equal floor(PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT / 2), the middle-of-bit sampling offset H, using integer division.

review.reason: Quote states LPARA_UART_HALF_BIT = floor(N/2) (REQ-PAR-002). It is an elaboration-time localparam, not checkable every cycle from interface signals, so assertion is wrong; verify via scenarios observing mid-bit sampling with odd and even N.

rules.quote: [REQ-PAR-001] The block shall behave as specified for every value of PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT from 4 to 65535 inclusive, both odd and even.
rules.condition: PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT is any value from 4 to 65535 inclusive, odd or even
rules.statement: The block shall behave as specified for every PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT value from 4 to 65535, both odd and even.

review.reason: Directly stated by REQ-PAR-001; exercised by scenarios across odd and even values.

rules.quote: [REQ-PAR-003] The block should stop elaboration with an error message when PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT is less than 4 or greater than 65535.
rules.condition: PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT is less than 4 or greater than 65535
rules.statement: The block should stop elaboration with an error message when PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT is outside 4 to 65535.

review.reason: REQ-PAR-003 is a SHOULD about an elaboration-time error; not checkable by simulation assertion or scenario, so check none is appropriate.

rules.quote: Port: i_rst_n; Direction: input; Width: 1; Signal type: Reset (asynchronous assertion, synchronous release); Reset value: Not applicable; Clock domain: CLK; Meaning: Active-low reset
rules.statement: i_rst_n is an active-low reset that asserts asynchronously and releases synchronously to i_clk.

review.reason: Quote states active-low reset, async assert, sync release; scenario check fine.

rules.quote: Port: i_tx_valid; Direction: input; Width: 1; Signal type: Data; Reset value: Not applicable; Clock domain: CLK; Meaning: Transmit stream: i_tx_data holds a byte to send Port: o_tx_ready; Direction: output; Width: 1; Signal type: Data; Reset value: 1; Clock domain: CLK; Meaning: Transmit stream: the transmitter can accept a byte at the next edge
rules.condition: o_tx_ready is high and i_tx_valid is high at a clock edge
rules.statement: When o_tx_ready is 1, the transmitter must accept the byte on i_tx_data at the next i_clk edge.

review.reason: Quote only says o_tx_ready means transmitter can accept a byte at next edge; handshake acceptance is a stream rule. Actor should be the transmitter slave, ok, but checkable from interface only partially (acceptance not visible). Scenario is right; keep the scenario check but the strength is a meaning statement, so SHOULD is not warranted. Keep MUST with scenario.

rules.quote: Port: o_tx_ready; Direction: output; Width: 1; Signal type: Data; Reset value: 1; Clock domain: CLK; Meaning: Transmit stream: the transmitter can accept a byte at the next edge
rules.statement: o_tx_ready must reset to 1.

review.reason: Reset value 1 stated; checkable after reset.

rules.quote: Port: i_tx_data; Direction: input; Width: 8; Signal type: Data; Reset value: Not applicable; Clock domain: CLK; Meaning: Transmit stream: byte to send; bit 0 is sent first
rules.statement: Bit 0 of i_tx_data must be sent first on o_txd.

review.reason: Bit 0 sent first is stated, but the transmitter on o_txd is the actor (slave of the tx stream), not source.

rules.quote: Port: o_rx_valid; Direction: output; Width: 1; Signal type: Data; Reset value: 0; Clock domain: CLK; Meaning: Receive stream: the holding register holds a byte
rules.statement: o_rx_valid must reset to 0.

review.reason: Reset value 0 stated.

rules.quote: Port: o_rx_valid; Direction: output; Width: 1; Signal type: Data; Reset value: 0; Clock domain: CLK; Meaning: Receive stream: the holding register holds a byte
rules.statement: o_rx_valid must be 1 when the holding register holds a byte.

review.reason: Meaning states o_rx_valid indicates holding register holds a byte; holding register is internal, so not checkable from interface; scenario is right. Actor is the receiver driving the stream (master/source).

rules.quote: Port: i_rx_ready; Direction: input; Width: 1; Signal type: Data; Reset value: Not applicable; Clock domain: CLK; Meaning: Receive stream: the consumer takes the held byte at this edge
rules.condition: i_rx_ready is high at a clock edge with o_rx_valid high
rules.statement: The held byte is taken by the consumer at the edge where i_rx_ready is 1.

review.reason: The consumer taking the byte at the i_rx_ready edge is a handshake; actor is the receiver driving o_rx_valid, which is the source.

rules.quote: Port: o_rx_data; Direction: output; Width: 8; Signal type: Data; Reset value: 0; Clock domain: CLK; Meaning: Receive stream: received byte; bit 0 was received first; qualified by o_rx_valid
rules.statement: o_rx_data must reset to 0.

review.reason: Reset value 0 stated; actor should be the source of the rx stream.

rules.quote: Port: o_rx_data; Direction: output; Width: 8; Signal type: Data; Reset value: 0; Clock domain: CLK; Meaning: Receive stream: received byte; bit 0 was received first; qualified by o_rx_valid
rules.statement: o_rx_data must present the received byte with bit 0 received first, qualified by o_rx_valid.

review.reason: Data content and bit order are stated; actor is the source of the rx stream.

rules.quote: Port: o_rx_frame_err; Direction: output; Width: 1; Signal type: Data; Reset value: 0; Clock domain: CLK; Meaning: Receive stream: 1 when the stop bit of the held byte was sampled as 0; qualified by o_rx_valid
rules.statement: o_rx_frame_err must reset to 0.

review.reason: Reset value 0 stated; actor should be source.

rules.quote: Port: o_rx_frame_err; Direction: output; Width: 1; Signal type: Data; Reset value: 0; Clock domain: CLK; Meaning: Receive stream: 1 when the stop bit of the held byte was sampled as 0; qualified by o_rx_valid
rules.statement: o_rx_frame_err must be 1 when the stop bit of the held byte was sampled as 0, qualified by o_rx_valid.

review.reason: Stated by quote; the stop bit sampling is internal so scenario check; actor is source.

rules.quote: Port: o_rx_overrun; Direction: output; Width: 1; Signal type: Data; Reset value: 0; Clock domain: CLK; Meaning: One-cycle pulse: a received byte was dropped because the holding register was full
rules.statement: o_rx_overrun must reset to 0.

review.reason: Reset value 0 stated; actor should be source.

rules.quote: Port: o_rx_overrun; Direction: output; Width: 1; Signal type: Data; Reset value: 0; Clock domain: CLK; Meaning: One-cycle pulse: a received byte was dropped because the holding register was full
rules.condition: a received byte is dropped because the holding register is full
rules.statement: o_rx_overrun must pulse for one cycle when a received byte is dropped because the holding register is full.

review.reason: One-cycle pulse is stated; actor is source; check should be scenario since the drop condition depends on internal state and needs stimulus.

rules.quote: Port: o_txd; Direction: output; Width: 1; Signal type: Data; Reset value: 1; Clock domain: CLK; Meaning: Serial transmit line, idle high
rules.statement: o_txd must reset to 1 and be high when idle.

review.reason: Reset value 1 and idle high are stated; actor is the transmitter (slave) of the tx stream, and idle-high is checkable only with knowledge of idle, so use scenario for idle; reset value is assertion. Use both.

rules.quote: Port: i_rxd; Direction: input; Width: 1; Signal type: Data (asynchronous); Reset value: Not applicable; Clock domain: ASYNC; Meaning: Serial receive line, idle high, asynchronous to i_clk, synchronised inside the block
rules.statement: i_rxd, asynchronous to i_clk and idle high, must be synchronised inside the block.

review.reason: Quote says the line is synchronised inside the block, an internal implementation detail; the input is driven by the environment, so the actor is the system and it is not directly verifiable at the interface. Keep as scenario with asynchronous stimulus.

rules.quote: [REQ-CLK-001] All state elements of the block shall be clocked by the rising edge of i_clk only, with no other clock, no gated clock and no latch.
rules.statement: All state elements shall be clocked only by the rising edge of i_clk, with no other clock, no gated clock and no latch.

review.reason: Quote states it. check=none is acceptable: structural clocking property, not observable from interface signals.

rules.quote: [REQ-RST-001] When i_rst_n becomes 0, every flip-flop of the block shall take its reset value at once, without waiting for an edge of i_clk.
rules.statement: Every flip-flop shall take its reset value at once, without waiting for an i_clk edge.

review.reason: Asynchronous reset behaviour is checkable by asserting outputs change immediately when i_rst_n falls, but the 'every flip-flop' internal state is not interface-visible; a scenario/assertion on outputs is fine. Keep as both is more accurate.

rules.quote: [REQ-RST-002] While i_rst_n is 0, the outputs shall have these values: o_txd = 1, o_tx_ready = 1, o_rx_valid = 0, o_rx_data = 0, o_rx_frame_err = 0, o_rx_overrun = 0.
rules.statement: Outputs shall be o_txd = 1, o_tx_ready = 1, o_rx_valid = 0, o_rx_data = 0, o_rx_frame_err = 0, o_rx_overrun = 0.

review.reason: Output values during reset are checkable every cycle from interface signals.

rules.quote: [REQ-RST-003] While i_rst_n is 0, no transmit byte shall be accepted, even when i_tx_valid = 1 and o_tx_ready = 1.
rules.condition: While i_rst_n is 0, even when i_tx_valid = 1 and o_tx_ready = 1
rules.statement: No transmit byte shall be accepted.

review.reason: Quote states it; checkable by assertion (e.g. o_txd stays 1) and by scenario driving i_tx_valid during reset.

rules.quote: [REQ-RST-004] While i_rst_n is 0, the receiver shall not detect a start bit and shall not deliver a byte.
rules.statement: The receiver shall not detect a start bit and shall not deliver a byte.

review.reason: Quote states it; checked by assertion on o_rx_valid and a scenario driving start bit during reset.

rules.quote: [REQ-RST-005] Both i_rxd synchronizer flip-flops, and any flip-flop that holds the previous synchronised line value, shall reset to 1.
rules.statement: Both i_rxd synchronizer flip-flops and any flip-flop holding the previous synchronised line value shall reset to 1.

review.reason: Quote states it; internal synchronizer reset values are verified by a scenario (first-edge start detection), not by interface assertion.

rules.quote: [REQ-RST-006] If reset is asserted during a transmission, the frame shall be abandoned: o_txd shall become 1 at once, and the rest of the frame and the byte shall not be sent after the release.
rules.statement: The frame shall be abandoned and o_txd shall become 1 at once.

review.reason: Rule text covers only the frame abandon and o_txd=1 at once; the 'not sent after release' part is split into UL-6.2-07. Fields fine (o_txd=1 immediate is assertion-checkable), keep as both.

merged_from.quote: [REQ-RST-006] If reset is asserted during a transmission, the frame shall be abandoned: o_txd shall become 1 at once, and the rest of the frame and the byte shall not be sent after the release.

rules.quote: [REQ-RST-007] If reset is asserted during a reception, the partly received frame shall be discarded and shall not produce o_rx_valid, o_rx_frame_err or o_rx_overrun after the release.
rules.statement: The partly received frame shall be discarded and shall not produce o_rx_valid, o_rx_frame_err or o_rx_overrun after the release.

review.reason: The rule is a prohibition: discarded frame must not produce o_rx_valid/frame_err/overrun after release. Strength should be MUST_NOT-like; it is written as MUST discard.

rules.quote: [REQ-RST-008] If reset is asserted while o_rx_valid = 1, the held byte shall be discarded.
rules.statement: The held byte shall be discarded.

review.reason: Quote states the held byte is discarded; verified by scenario (o_rx_valid/data after reset).

rules.quote: [REQ-RST-009] After the release of i_rst_n, the transmitter shall be idle with o_tx_ready = 1, and it shall be able to accept a byte at the first edge after the release.
rules.statement: The transmitter shall be idle with o_tx_ready = 1 and shall accept a byte at the first edge after the release.

review.reason: Quote states it; o_tx_ready=1 is assertion-checkable and acceptance at first edge by scenario.

rules.quote: [REQ-RST-010] After the release of i_rst_n, the receiver shall be idle.
rules.statement: The receiver shall be idle.

review.reason: Quote states it; receiver idle verified by scenario.

rules.quote: For the first edge R1 after the release, s(R1-1) shall be taken as 1 (the reset value of the synchronizer). So if s(R1) = 0, R1 is detected as T0 (Section 10.5).
rules.condition: First edge R1 after reset release
rules.statement: The previous synchronised value s(R1-1) shall be taken as 1, so s(R1) = 0 is detected as T0.

review.reason: Quote states it; scenario with i_rxd=0 at first edge after release.

rules.quote: [REQ-GEN-001] The block shall send and receive frames in 8N1 format: a start bit of value 0, then eight data bits with the least significant bit first, then a stop bit of value 1, with no parity bit.
rules.statement: Frames shall be sent and received in 8N1 format: start bit 0, eight data bits LSB first, stop bit 1, no parity bit.

review.reason: Stated by quote.

rules.quote: [REQ-GEN-002] The transmitter and the receiver shall work at the same time and independently.
rules.statement: The transmitter and receiver shall operate simultaneously and independently.

review.reason: Stated by quote.

rules.quote: No activity of one shall change the timing or the outputs of the other.
rules.statement: Activity of the transmitter shall not change the timing or outputs of the receiver, and vice versa.

review.reason: Stated by quote.

rules.quote: [REQ-GEN-003] Every output port shall be driven directly by a flip-flop clocked by i_clk, so there is no combinational path from any input port to any output port.
rules.statement: Every output port shall be driven directly by a flip-flop clocked by i_clk, with no combinational path from any input to any output.

review.reason: Observable: outputs change only after clock edges.

rules.quote: [REQ-TX-001] The transmitter shall accept a byte at an edge only when, at that edge, i_tx_valid = 1, o_tx_ready = 1 and i_rst_n = 1.
rules.statement: The transmitter shall accept a byte at an edge only when i_tx_valid = 1, o_tx_ready = 1 and i_rst_n = 1.

review.reason: 'Only when' restricts acceptance, so it is a prohibition.

rules.quote: [REQ-TX-002] The transmitter shall capture i_tx_data at the accepting edge E0. The value of i_tx_data at any other edge shall have no effect.
rules.statement: The transmitter shall capture i_tx_data at the accepting edge E0; i_tx_data at any other edge shall have no effect.

review.reason: Stated by quote.

rules.quote: [REQ-TX-003] While the transmitter is idle (no frame in progress), o_tx_ready shall be 1.
rules.condition: transmitter idle, no frame in progress
rules.statement: o_tx_ready shall be 1 while the transmitter is idle.

review.reason: Stated by quote.

rules.quote: [REQ-TX-004] After an accepting edge E0, o_tx_ready shall be 0 in the cycles after edges E0 to E0+10N-2 inclusive.
rules.statement: o_tx_ready shall be 0 in the cycles after edges E0 to E0+10N-2 inclusive.

review.reason: Stated by quote.

rules.quote: [REQ-TX-005] After an accepting edge E0, o_tx_ready shall become 1 at edge E0+10N-1, which is the last cycle of the stop bit.
rules.statement: o_tx_ready shall become 1 at edge E0+10N-1, the last cycle of the stop bit.

review.reason: Stated by quote.

rules.quote: [REQ-TX-006] If i_tx_valid is 0 at an edge, or o_tx_ready is 0 at that edge, the transmitter shall not accept a byte and its state shall not depend on i_tx_data.
rules.condition: i_tx_valid is 0 or o_tx_ready is 0 at an edge
rules.statement: The transmitter shall not accept a byte and its state shall not depend on i_tx_data.

review.reason: Stated by quote.

rules.quote: [REQ-TX-007] The transmitter shall not require i_tx_valid to stay 1 until a handshake. If i_tx_valid returns to 0 before a handshake, nothing is sent.
rules.statement: The transmitter shall not require i_tx_valid to stay 1 until a handshake; if it returns to 0 before a handshake, nothing is sent.

review.reason: Stated by quote.

rules.quote: [REQ-TX-008] The transmitter shall hold at most one byte, the byte being sent, and shall have no transmit buffer beyond it.
rules.statement: The transmitter shall hold at most one byte, the one being sent, with no additional transmit buffer.

review.reason: Stated by quote; exercised by trying to push a second byte while busy.

rules.quote: Frame bit j (j = 0 to 9) of a byte D is: bit 0 = 0 (start bit); bit j = D[j-1] for j = 1 to 8; bit 9 = 1 (stop bit). [REQ-TX-010] For a byte D accepted at edge E0, o_txd in the cycle after edge E0+k shall equal frame bit floor(k / N) of D, for every k from 0 to 10N-1.
rules.condition: byte D accepted at edge E0
rules.statement: o_txd in the cycle after edge E0+k shall equal frame bit floor(k/N) of D (bit0=0, bit j=D[j-1], bit9=1) for k from 0 to 10N-1.

review.reason: Stated by quote.

merged_from.quote: [REQ-TX-011] Each of the 10 frame bits shall be driven on o_txd for exactly N consecutive cycles.

rules.quote: [REQ-TX-012] If a new byte is accepted at edge E0+10N, its start bit shall begin at edge E0+10N, with no idle cycle between the stop bit of the previous frame and the new start bit.
rules.condition: new byte accepted at edge E0+10N
rules.statement: The start bit of the new frame shall begin at edge E0+10N with no idle cycle after the previous stop bit.

review.reason: Stated by quote.

rules.quote: [REQ-TX-013] If no byte is accepted at edge E0+10N, o_txd shall be 1 from edge E0+10N until the edge after which the next accepted frame starts.
rules.condition: no byte accepted at edge E0+10N
rules.statement: o_txd shall be 1 from edge E0+10N until the edge after which the next accepted frame starts.

review.reason: Stated by quote.

rules.quote: [REQ-TX-014] While the transmitter is idle, o_txd shall be 1.
rules.statement: o_txd shall be 1 while the transmitter is idle.

review.reason: Stated by quote.

rules.section_title: Receive line synchronisation and start detection
rules.quote: [REQ-RX-001] i_rxd shall go through a synchronizer of exactly two flip-flops clocked by i_clk, with no logic between them, before any other logic of the block uses it.
rules.statement: i_rxd shall pass through a synchronizer of exactly two flip-flops clocked by i_clk, with no logic between them, before other logic uses it.

review.reason: Stated by quote; checked via sampling latency.

rules.section_title: Receive line synchronisation and start detection
rules.quote: [REQ-RX-002] The receiver shall be in one of two conditions, idle or receiving. It shall be idle after reset, after a glitch (REQ-RX-005) and after the stop-bit sample of a frame (REQ-RX-013).
rules.statement: The receiver shall be either idle or receiving, and shall be idle after reset, after a glitch and after the stop-bit sample of a frame.

review.reason: Stated by quote.

rules.section_title: Receive line synchronisation and start detection
rules.quote: [REQ-RX-003] While idle, the receiver shall detect a start bit at edge T0 if and only if s(T0-1) = 1 and s(T0) = 0.
rules.statement: The receiver shall detect a start bit at edge T0 if and only if s(T0-1)=1 and s(T0)=0.

review.reason: Stated by quote.

rules.section_title: Receive line synchronisation and start detection
rules.quote: [REQ-RX-004] The receiver shall not need the line to be high for longer than the single sample s(T0-1) = 1 before a start bit.
rules.statement: The receiver shall not need the line high longer than the single sample s(T0-1)=1 before a start bit.

review.reason: Stated by quote.

rules.section_title: Receive line synchronisation and start detection
rules.quote: [REQ-RX-005] At edge T0+H the receiver shall check the start bit. If s(T0+H) = 1, the receiver shall treat the event as a glitch, return to idle and receive no byte.
rules.statement: At T0+H the receiver shall check the start bit; if s(T0+H)=1 it shall treat it as a glitch, return to idle and receive no byte.

review.reason: Stated by quote.

rules.section_title: Receive line synchronisation and start detection
rules.quote: [REQ-RX-006] A glitch shall not change o_rx_valid, o_rx_data or o_rx_frame_err, and it shall not make o_rx_overrun pulse.
rules.statement: A glitch shall not change o_rx_valid, o_rx_data or o_rx_frame_err, and shall not make o_rx_overrun pulse.

review.reason: Stated by quote.

rules.section_title: Receive line synchronisation and start detection
rules.quote: [REQ-RX-007] After a glitch checked at edge T0+H, the receiver shall detect a new start bit at any edge T0' > T0+H at which REQ-RX-003 holds.
rules.condition: after a glitch checked at T0+H
rules.statement: The receiver shall detect a new start bit at any edge T0' > T0+H at which the start condition holds.

review.reason: Stated by quote.

rules.section_title: Receive line synchronisation and start detection
rules.quote: [REQ-RX-008] If s(T0+H) = 0, the receiver shall go on to receive the frame.
rules.statement: The receiver shall go on to receive the frame.

review.reason: Stated by quote.

rules.quote: [REQ-RX-010] For a frame detected at T0 and confirmed at T0+H, the receiver shall sample data bit i (i = 0 to 7) at edge T0+H+(i+1)N. The received byte bit i shall be s(T0+H+(i+1)N).
rules.condition: frame detected at T0 and confirmed at T0+H
rules.statement: Data bit i (0 to 7) shall be sampled at edge T0+H+(i+1)N, and received byte bit i shall equal s(T0+H+(i+1)N).

review.reason: Stated by quote.

rules.quote: [REQ-RX-011] The receiver shall sample the stop bit at edge M = T0+H+9N.
rules.statement: The receiver shall sample the stop bit at edge M = T0+H+9N.

review.reason: Stated by quote.

rules.quote: [REQ-RX-012] Only the samples s(T0-1), s(T0), s(T0+H), the eight data-bit samples and s(M) shall affect the result of a frame. Values of i_rxd at all other edges between T0 and M shall be ignored.
rules.statement: Only s(T0-1), s(T0), s(T0+H), the eight data samples and s(M) shall affect a frame result; i_rxd at other edges between T0 and M shall be ignored.

review.reason: Stated by quote.

rules.quote: [REQ-RX-013] Once it has sampled the stop bit at M, the receiver shall be idle. It shall detect a new start bit at any edge T0' > M at which REQ-RX-003 holds, including T0' = M+1 when s(M) = 1 and s(M+1) = 0.
rules.statement: The receiver shall be idle after sampling at M and shall detect a new start bit at any T0' > M where the start condition holds, including M+1.

review.reason: Stated by quote.

rules.quote: [REQ-RX-014] Every frame confirmed at T0+H shall complete at M, whatever the value of s(M).
rules.statement: Every confirmed frame shall complete at M regardless of the value of s(M).

review.reason: Stated by quote.

rules.quote: [REQ-RX-015] The receiver shall keep sampling and receiving frames while a byte is waiting in the holding register. A low i_rx_ready shall not stall or delay the receiver.
rules.statement: The receiver shall keep sampling and receiving frames; a low i_rx_ready shall not stall or delay it.

review.reason: Stated by quote.

questions.question: ENV-004 requires i_rxd to change away from rising clock edges. The loopback test (UL-12.3-03) connects o_txd to i_rxd, and o_txd changes synchronously with the clock. Is the loopback exempt from ENV-004, or is a delay or falling-edge offset required?
questions.note: The spec does not say whether the loopback test is exempt from ENV-004, or whether a delay or falling-edge offset is needed on the o_txd to i_rxd connection. The designer must decide this.

decision.answer: Not exempt. In the loopback test o_txd reaches i_rxd through a half-cycle delay (i_rxd changes at the falling edge of i_clk), so ENV-004 holds; no other delay is required.

questions.question: UL-12.2-02 asks for lint or structural review of the synchronizer. Who owns that check, and how does it fit the simulation verification flow?
questions.note: The spec says the synchronizer structure is checked by lint or structural review. It does not name an owner or say how that check fits into the simulation verification flow. The designer must decide this.

decision.answer: The synchronizer structure (two flip-flops in series on i_rxd, nothing else in between) is checked on the RTL at gate D2 (docs/RTL_RULES.md RR-33, with nnc rtl-check), not by simulation. Simulation checks only its port-visible effect (the receive latency of D-003).

answered_questions.question: When a received byte is dropped due to overrun, is the holding register's existing byte and its frame_err kept unchanged, and is the new byte entirely discarded?
answered_questions.answer: Yes. The new byte and its frame-error flag are dropped. The held byte, o_rx_data and o_rx_frame_err stay unchanged.

answered_questions.question: Is o_rx_overrun a one-cycle pulse, and is it a primary output not listed in the interface rule for the receive stream?
answered_questions.answer: Yes, o_rx_overrun is 1 for exactly one cycle. It is a separate output port, listed in the port table and in the features, and not part of the receive-stream tuple. It is not qualified by o_rx_valid.

answered_questions.question: Is a byte with a frame error still delivered with o_rx_valid asserted (quote says delivered together with the byte)?
answered_questions.answer: Yes. A frame-error byte is delivered with o_rx_valid=1, held and taken like any other byte. o_rx_frame_err=1 is delivered with it.

answered_questions.question: UL-4-01 gives the legal range 4 to 65535 while UL-4-04 only says SHOULD stop elaboration outside it. What is the defined behavior for out-of-range values if the elaboration check is absent? Also, is the 16-bit upper bound consistent with the counter width used for N?
answered_questions.answer: Behaviour for illegal values is unspecified and not verified. The elaboration error is only recommended (should). The range 4 to 65535 fits within a 16-bit counter, and the counters need be at most 16 bits wide.

answered_questions.question: For odd N, floor(N/2) puts the sample point one cycle before the true bit center. Is that acceptable for the receiver's timing and tolerance?
answered_questions.answer: Yes. H=floor(N/2) is the defined sampling offset. For odd N it is a defined point (N=5 gives H=2). No tolerance beyond what follows from the sampling points is claimed.

answered_questions.question: Is o_rx_valid/o_rx_data/o_rx_frame_err reset-value assertion meaningful when the reset is asserted asynchronously, and does reset clear them immediately?
answered_questions.answer: Yes. Reset assertion is asynchronous. Every flip-flop takes its reset value at once, without waiting for a clock edge. While reset is low, o_rx_valid, o_rx_data and o_rx_frame_err are 0.

answered_questions.question: Are the master/slave/source/destination roles for the tx and rx streams defined (which side drives valid and which drives ready)?
answered_questions.answer: Yes. For transmit, the upstream side drives i_tx_valid and i_tx_data, and the block drives o_tx_ready. For receive, the block drives o_rx_valid and the data, and the consumer drives i_rx_ready.

answered_questions.question: Does o_rx_frame_err hold its value while o_rx_valid is low, or is it don't-care?
answered_questions.answer: It holds. While o_rx_valid=0, o_rx_data and o_rx_frame_err keep the values of the last loaded byte, or 0 if none has been loaded since reset.

answered_questions.question: REQ-RST-001 says every flip-flop resets asynchronously, but REQ-RST-005/RST-009 and 'first edge after release' imply synchronous release handling. Is i_rst_n release synchronised internally or asserted/released asynchronously relative to i_clk?
answered_questions.answer: Reset assertion is asynchronous. Release is synchronised outside the block by the environment (ENV-001). The block has no reset synchronizer.

answered_questions.question: Does 'no transmit byte accepted while i_rst_n = 0' with o_tx_ready = 1 conflict with the handshake definition that a transfer happens when i_tx_valid and o_tx_ready are both 1?
answered_questions.answer: No conflict. The handshake definition itself includes i_rst_n=1, so no handshake can occur while reset is low even though o_tx_ready=1.

answered_questions.question: o_tx_ready is 0 in the cycles after E0..E0+10N-2 and 'becomes 1 at edge E0+10N-1'. Is ready first 1 in the cycle after edge E0+10N-1, so a new accept at E0+10N gives back-to-back frames? State the cycle convention precisely.
answered_questions.answer: A registered output that becomes X at edge E has value X in the cycle after edge E. o_tx_ready is 0 in the cycles after E0 to E0+10N-2. It becomes 1 at edge E0+10N-1, so it is 1 in the cycle after that edge, which is the last stop-bit cycle. A new byte can then be accepted at E0+10N, with its start bit beginning there and no idle cycle.

answered_questions.question: What are the value and constraints of H (half-bit) relative to N, e.g. for odd N or N=1? Does N=1 still work with the 2-flop synchronizer and the delivery at M+2?
answered_questions.answer: H=floor(N/2). For odd N it rounds down (N=5 gives H=2). N=1 is illegal, since the legal range is 4 to 65535, so it is not supported. Delivery is at V=M+2.

answered_questions.question: What happens to a frame in progress and to the holding register when i_rst_n is asserted? The spec only says a frame cut short by reset must not pulse overrun. Is the TX frame also aborted, and does o_txd return to 1?
answered_questions.answer: A TX frame in progress is abandoned. o_txd becomes 1 at once and the byte is lost. A partly received frame is discarded and gives no valid, frame_err or overrun after release. A held byte is discarded.

answered_questions.question: If the next frame completes at M' before the previous frame's delivery edge V=M+2 (possible for small N), is delivery of both frames still ordered and each checked at its own V?
answered_questions.answer: Yes. Each frame is delivered at its own V=M+2, in completion order. After M the receiver is idle, so the next start is at T0'>M and the spacing between starts is at least H+9N+1 cycles. With N at least 4, the next frame's M' therefore falls well after V.

answered_questions.question: Are 'master' and 'slave' the correct actor labels for the UART transmitter and receiver? UL-8.1-xx and UL-8.2-xx describe a transmitter and a receiver, not bus master and slave roles.
answered_questions.answer: No. The spec uses transmitter and receiver, with valid/ready streams. Neither master nor slave appears as a role.

answered_questions.question: UL-8.1-01 says the start bit starts at E0 and also that this is the first cycle after the handshake. Is the start bit visible on o_txd during the cycle that follows E0, or is it visible at E0 itself?
answered_questions.answer: The start bit is on o_txd in the cycle after edge E0 (k=0), which is the first cycle after the handshake. It is a registered output, not visible at E0 itself.

answered_questions.question: What are H and M? The quotes don't define H, the half-bit offset, or M, the stop-bit sample point. For odd N, how is H rounded?
answered_questions.answer: H=floor(N/2), the offset of the middle-of-bit sample, so odd N rounds down. M=T0+H+9N is the stop-bit sampling edge.

answered_questions.question: Is a dropped byte's frame error never reported on o_rx_frame_err, and is the overrun-with-frame-error case in the stuck-low scenario consistent with it?
answered_questions.answer: Yes. The frame error of a dropped byte is not reported. In the stuck-low case the spec allows either delivery of 0x00 with frame_err=1 or a drop with an overrun pulse, so it is consistent.

answered_questions.question: What is the exact definition of 'sampled as 1 then as 0' for re-arming after a stuck-low frame, e.g. is a single 1 sample enough?
answered_questions.answer: A start bit needs s=1 at one edge and s=0 at the next. A single sample of 1 followed by 0 is enough, and no longer high time is needed.

answered_questions.question: The sampling-point test (UL-12.3-01) needs the wrong value at the edges just before and after the sampling edge. For small N, such as N=1 or 2, does this apply, or are some bits skipped? The spec only says 'where N allows that'.
answered_questions.answer: N=1 and N=2 are illegal, since N is at least 4, so they are not tested. At N=4 the sample is 2 edges after the first edge of the bit and 1 edge before its last, so edges just before and after exist.

answered_questions.question: Does 'all flip-flops use asynchronous reset' also cover the two i_rxd synchronizer flops, and is reset deassertion assumed to be synchronized externally?
answered_questions.answer: Yes. All flip-flops use the asynchronous active-low reset, including both synchronizer flops, which reset to 1. Reset release is synchronised externally by the environment.

answered_questions.question: What does 'legal value' of PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT mean (the minimum and maximum)? The quotes don't give the range.
answered_questions.answer: The legal range is 4 to 65535 inclusive. The default is 16.

answered_questions.question: UL-14-09: what does 'a byte is dropped' mean (overrun when the held byte is not taken?), and how is the frame-error of a dropped byte observed, since the output holds the last loaded values (UL-14-07)?
answered_questions.answer: A byte is dropped when a frame completes at V while o_rx_valid=1 and i_rx_ready=0, which gives an overrun. The frame-error flag of a dropped byte is not reported, so it is not observable.

answered_questions.question: UL-14-01 and UL-14-08: is o_tx_ready 1 immediately on reset assertion (asynchronous) or only after the next clock edge? Likewise for o_txd=1 'at once'.
answered_questions.answer: Yes, both are immediate. On reset assertion every flip-flop takes its reset value at once, without a clock edge. So o_tx_ready=1 and o_txd=1 immediately.
